full_judgment:
3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement along with two sets of additional better statements controverting the averments made in the plaint. They contended, inter alia, that the defendants entered into an agreement for sale (bainapatra) of their property to the plaintiff. Subsequently, the plaintiff considering her financial capacity agreed to execute and register sale deed of land measuring (16½  decimals out of land mentioned in the bainapatra and 66 decimals of land) in total 82½ decimals and nominated her husband Mr. Syed Al Faruque, and a deed was executed on 08.06.2000 and registered on 11.6.2000 in favour of the plaintiff. In this way the defendants adjusted the whole amount of the earnest money and other money paid by the plaintiff. The possession of the land was also handed over to the plaintiff. The plaintiff's case is barred by Article 113 of the Limitation Act. It would be evidenced from the prayer for recovery of khas possession of the land in the plaint that the defendant is in possession of the suit land. It is admitted in the plaint that part performance of bainapatra has been fulfilled and in that case as per section 63 of the Contract Act the bainapatra became ineffective. The bainapatra on the face of it lost its legal character in the absence of its scribe, stamp buyer and for including the names of two dead persons in the agreement. 

 9. The High Court Division also considered the evidence and materials on record and noted that P.W. 1 in his deposition admitted that at the time of execution of bainapatra the suit land was handed over to the plaintiff. He also admitted that the bainapatra was partially executed. However, noting that the plaintiff had prayed for recovery of khas possession, the trial Court did not believe that the plaintiff had possession over all of the suit land. Upon assessing the totality of the evidence, the High Court Division also accepted that the earnest money paid in respect of the bainapatra was adjusted upon registering 82½ decimals of land of which 16½ decimals was from land mentioned in the bainapatra, the effect of the bainapatra came to an end.
